label: r2c2
name: Shifted input, 1 PPO epoch
hypothesis: Same as r1c1, but with ppo_epochs 1. That gives about 3.25x the samples (about 425k steps) for a similar number of gradient steps. Together with the 2-epoch trial it shows which way to move on epochs. Fresh, varied designs should generalise better to held-out targets than reusing data. Refuted if it scores below both the 2-epoch candidate and r1c1 (about 0.59), which would mean one epoch learns too little from each sample.
last_analysis: The X/2 input shift makes the task learnable. Moving to 1 PPO epoch for about 3x more samples gave the best result: r2c2 at 0.936, with both seeds high. Most failures now come from a few unlucky seeds. Three runs scored exactly 0.0781 on one seed. Where readouts exist, the agent fills only the ground layer, then picks DONE (IoU 0.714). Bad seeds appear with more gradient steps per sample (r3c1) and longer horizons (gamma 0.99 in r3c3, which picked DONE at once). A bigger trunk cost samples and hurt (r3c2). The remaining gains likely come from making early training reliable, not from more capacity. So each candidate makes one change to r2c2 aimed at stable early learning: lower gamma, near-zero starting action scores (a standard initialisation), or fewer, larger minibatches.
